## Historical audit — S0340

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/selection/bw_0017/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible; citations below refer to its JSONL events.

The requested goal was a photo-matched, editable Blender reconstruction. The student’s *interpretation* was an industrial workshop with a raised processing line, stairs, tank and conveyor; the reference image itself is not visible to this audit (line 1; H response, line 3).

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H produced a complete SceneAct program with separate architecture, multiple machines, ductwork, tank, stairs and conveyor parts. It specified colored surfaces, metallic and roughness settings, camera, world and lights; no image textures are evident in the code. Rods and elbows, stair supports and rails were explicitly modeled, but their physical connectivity and visual correctness were not independently checked (H response line 3; execute line 4). |
| First validation | Build and render completed with return code 0; step 1 was selected (lines 6, 8–10). The numerical window projection was `(0.382, 0.35)` against H’s estimated `(0.10, 0.34)`, and the conveyor endpoint was `(0.072, 0.673)` against `(0.02, 0.94)` (line 9). These are point comparisons, not silhouette or visibility verification. |
| Review and revision | The runner supplied the reference, rendered view and comparison instructions (H request line 11). H claimed the render showed the hall exterior, small distant equipment, excessive floor and obstructing posts. It moved the camera inside, enlarged the hall, relocated glazing and revised equipment while retaining multiple assets (H response line 13; execute line 14). Those visual claims are H’s, not independently verified here. |
| Second validation | Build and render again completed; step 2 was selected (lines 16, 18–20). The selected window and conveyor landmark projections were outside the image horizontally, at `(-0.115, 0.392)` and `(-0.423, 1.008)`. An upward-aim trial moved their projected y values downward and was restored (lines 14, 19). Different landmark locations and changed geometry limit direct cross-build comparison. |
| Further exploration | After receiving the second result and images (H request line 21), H described a thin foreground strip, misplaced tank and low machine, then produced a third program raising and shifting local objects, adding a conveyor lane and open frames, moving the window wall and testing a lower camera aim (H response line 23). **Execution or validation of this third program is not visible.** |

**Teacher input:** No separate teacher detection, diagnosis or proposed patch is visible in this chunk. The runner’s review instructions were actually presented, and H’s subsequent comparison and revision show engagement with them; this does not establish receipt of any separate teacher advice. The model sessions report no observed tool calls, while the external runner performed the recorded Blender executions (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Two builds and renders succeeded technically, but overall scene fidelity and final submission are **unknown**. There is no visible formal success verdict, algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption. Camera pose, object proportions, connections, materials, lighting and render appearance cannot be verified without the images; H’s descriptions are not independent verification. The transferable observation is that numerical projections exposed discrepancies yet did not establish visible contours. The particular camera and asset adjustments are task-specific hypotheses, not proven improvements. Later events in the unseen chunk remain unknown.
